summary: Fourteen days of Nightscout data with high CGM quality (98.7 percent coverage, 5-minute cadence, 3995 valid entries, no invalid or duplicate records). Overall glucose metrics are good: mean 121.6 mg/dL, time in range 86.0 percent, coefficient of variation 32.6 percent. Time below range is 5.1 percent, above the commonly cited 4 percent threshold, and hypoglycemia is clustered rather than random: 18:00-19:00 local (time below range 7.7 and 15.3 percent, minima 42 and 41 mg/dL) and 23:00-03:00 local (10.1 to 18.5 percent). The highest glucose block is 13:00-17:00 local (mean 135.0 to 162.8 mg/dL, time above range 16.6 to 32.1 percent). No carbohydrate entries exist in the period (carb_entries 0, total_carbs_g 0.0, COB 0 in all sampled loop statuses), and the user-declared meal_strategies list is empty, so all meal coverage is delivered by UAM. Insulin-on-board reached 4.73 U and 5.935 U with no carbohydrate on board, and dynamic sensitivity values ranged from 27.8 to 124 mg/dL per unit around a flat profile ISF of 56 mg/dL per unit. Two safety limits (max IOB 25 U, max basal 12 U/h) never bind at this insulin scale. Device events (occlusion and pump error on 08-19, three site changes, two sensor changes) and three logged GLP-1 doses add non-stationarity that limits attribution of individual days to profile settings.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM data are suitable for hourly and daily pattern work: 3995 valid entries, 0 invalid, 0 duplicate, 0 out-of-period, estimated cadence 5.0 minutes, coverage 98.7 percent of 4046 expected entries, 10 gaps with a largest gap of 65 minutes. The first day (2026-08-07) has only 33 readings and is weighted down. Local time context is unambiguous (BST, +60 minutes, device-sourced), and hourly_glucose_local is a clean +1 hour shift of hourly_glucose, so all time-of-day reasoning uses local rows. The AAPS profile is structurally complete: 7 basal segments, 5 carb-ratio segments, 1 ISF segment, 3 target segments, DIA, and a full SMB and limits block; profile_context states historical_applicability yes, so the profile is treated as valid for the whole window. Carbohydrate telemetry is entirely absent (carb_entries 0, total_carbs_g 0.0, carb_treatment_entries empty, extended_carb_entries 0, COB 0 in all 24 sampled loop statuses). Only 40 of 2315 treatments and 24 of 6214 device statuses are exposed, so loop-reason patterns are illustrative rather than statistically representative. It is not stated whether total_insulin_u of 275.95 U includes basal delivery, which changes the implied daily dose materially. Confounders inside the window: profile switch on 08-13, site changes 08-10, 08-13 and 08-17, sensor changes 08-11 and 08-21, occlusion and pump error on 08-19, and GLP-1 1.25 mg notes on 08-14, 08-17 and 08-20.

analysis_steps.dependencies: None; this is the root stage that constrains every later inference.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carbohydrate records; no split of total_insulin_u into basal and bolus; no activity or exercise log; no insulin peak time despite insulin_type free_peak_oref; no pump concentration field to confirm the dilution implied by the profile-switch note.

analysis_steps.findings: Aggregate metrics are largely at target (time in range 86.0 percent, coefficient of variation 32.6 percent, standard deviation 39.7) but time below range of 5.1 percent exceeds the usual 4 percent goal, and the hypoglycemia is time-clustered. Evening cluster: 18:00 local time below range 7.7 percent with minimum 42 mg/dL and 19:00 local 15.3 percent with minimum 41 mg/dL. Late-night cluster: 23:00 through 03:00 local shows 10.1, 11.4, 18.5, 10.1 and 10.2 percent below range. Three level-2 episodes are documented: 08-13 dropping 51 to 42 mg/dL at 18:00-18:15 local, 08-14 dropping 48 to 41 mg/dL at 19:05-19:15 local, and 08-21 at 42 mg/dL at 07:19 local. Severe hyperglycemia clusters at 285-293 mg/dL on 08-15 around 17:30 local and on 08-18 around 12:55-13:15 local. The worst days combine both extremes (08-14: in range 70.8, above 20.8, below 8.3 percent; 08-18: in range 71.9, above 15.3, below 12.8 percent), indicating swing rather than a uniform offset. Loop statuses show a repeated over-delivery signature: minGuardBG -4 with a 120-minute zero temp on 08-11, minGuardBG -59 with a 120-minute zero temp on 08-16, and minGuardBG 28 with a 120-minute zero temp on 08-20. Response windows show very large falls after very small user doses, so the fall is automation-driven: 0.2 U from 234 mg/dL producing -178 mg/dL at 120 minutes on 08-14, 0.2 U from 172 mg/dL producing -125 mg/dL at 240 minutes on 08-13, and 0.65 U from 264 mg/dL producing -168 mg/dL at 120 minutes on 08-19. The final status of the window shows glucose 245.7 mg/dL rising with IOB 5.935 U, variable sensitivity 27.8 mg/dL per unit, insulin request 2.12 U and rate 4 U/h, which is a substantial forward hypoglycemia exposure after the data end. Configured ceilings (max IOB 25 U, max basal 12 U/h) are permissive relative to this insulin scale. The occlusion and pump error on 08-19 precede that day's high glucose, so that day must not be attributed to profile settings.

analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carbohydrate or activity annotation for the 14:00-19:00 local block; no rescue-carbohydrate records, so it cannot be established whether the 41-47 mg/dL episodes were treated or resolved spontaneously.

analysis_steps.findings: The most fasting-like window, 04:00-08:00 local, is the best-controlled part of the day: averages 106.0, 104.2, 99.5, 99.5 and 110.5 mg/dL, time in range 95.8 to 98.7 percent, time below range 0.0 to 4.8 percent, and no time above range. The dawn-side basal shape (0.7 U/h from 05:00 and 0.8 U/h from 06:00) matches this window well; the single 42 mg/dL at 07:19 local on 08-21 is isolated. The 23:00-03:00 local block declines to means of 105.7, 93.3, 90.6, 101.9 and 104.7 mg/dL with time below range up to 18.5 percent, then recovers spontaneously by 04:00. This descending-then-recovering shape is equally consistent with an insulin-action tail under DIA 10 h, with a slightly high early-night basal of 0.6 U/h, and with the tight 90 mg/dL target from 23:00 leaving no buffer; these three explanations are not separated by the available data. The 13:00-17:00 local block is the worst for hyperglycemia (means 135.0, 148.1, 153.0, 162.8, 148.9 mg/dL; time above range 16.6, 26.3, 23.6, 32.1, 22.6 percent) and the scheduled basal is at its lowest there (0.5 U/h from 16:00). This is suggestive but cannot be called a basal defect, because with zero carbohydrate entries and COB always 0, unannounced meals are at least as plausible, and both 285-293 mg/dL clusters fall in or near this band on days with device or GLP-1 confounders. The 18:00-19:00 local block is the mirror image: means fall from 162.8 to 148.9 to 124.2 to 105.4 mg/dL while time below range rises to 7.7 and 15.3 percent, and the scheduled basal rises there (0.6 U/h from 18:00, 0.7 U/h from 19:00), adding basal into the falling limb. Targets of 90, 100 and 90 mg/dL are tight; loop statuses show effective targets moving between 80 and 116 mg/dL, and the user set 135 mg/dL temporary targets on six occasions, several lasting 180 minutes, which is independent evidence that the standing target feels too low in specific windows. Delivered temp basal rates in the sample range from 0 to 4.0 U/h against a scheduled 0.5-0.8 U/h, so scheduled basal is not the same as delivered basal and hourly averages cannot be read as a direct basal test.
analysis_steps.evidence: hourly_glucose_local, all 24 rows; aaps_profile.basal_segments (0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.7, 0.5, 0.6, 0.7 U/h) summing to 16.2 U/day; aaps_profile.target_segments (90, 100, 90 mg/dL); representative_events (six temporary targets, five at 135 mg/dL); representative_treatments (temp basal rates 0 to 3.6 U/h); representative_loop_statuses (08-14 18:40 clamp to maxSafeBasal 4).

analysis_steps.data_gaps: No meal markers; no delivered-basal time series beyond 40 sampled treatments; no activity log to explain the intent of the 16:00 local basal trough; the 14-day hourly aggregate mixes days before and after the 08-13 profile switch and before and after GLP-1 dosing.

analysis_steps.findings: Carb ratios (13, 11.1, 13.2, 10.5 and 12.6 g/U) cannot be validated at all: with carb_entries 0 and COB 0 in every sampled status, no carb ratio was exercised during the period. Carb-ratio values appear in loop reason strings only as profile read-back. ISF is a single flat segment of 56 mg/dL per unit, but delivered sensitivity is dynamic and very wide: sampled variable sensitivity values are 124, 111.9, 108.4, 101.2, 95.1, 88.3, 87.1, 86.9, 83.3, 83.0, 81.9, 76.3, 71.6, 71.0, 68.1, 58.9, 54.2, 53.4, 51.9, 43.2, 42.5, 37.9 and 27.8 mg/dL per unit, a roughly 4.5-fold spread around 56, produced by dynamic_sensitivity_enabled true with a 70 percent adjustment factor while autosens_enabled is false. The spread is glucose-dependent in the aggressive direction: 27.8 mg/dL per unit at 245.7 mg/dL and 37.9 at 262.2 mg/dL, versus 124 at 69.8 mg/dL and 111.9 at 95.1 mg/dL. Because dynamic ISF continuously rescales the profile value, the flat ISF of 56 and the 70 percent adjustment factor are partially interchangeable levers acting on the same output, and changing both would make the result uninterpretable. DIA of 10 hours pairs with insulin_type free_peak_oref, and several response windows show continued decline at 240-360 minutes after very small doses (08-17 21:15: 125 to 57 mg/dL at 240 minutes and 75 at 360; 08-12 21:30: 138 to 82 at 240 and 87 at 360; 08-16 15:45: 206 to 53 at 180). These windows contain concurrent temp-basal and SMB delivery, so they demonstrate net system action rather than an insulin curve, and DIA cannot be quantitatively validated. Insulin scale check: scheduled basal is 16.2 U/day while total_insulin_u is 275.95 U over 14 days (about 19.7 U/day), and 655 insulin entries over 14 days is about 47 per day, consistent with an SMB-dominant system; whether the 275.95 U figure includes basal remains unresolved and is the single most valuable clarification for this stage. The loop reason strings contain non-stock markers (UAM Boost 1 and 2, UAM High Boost enacted, Enhanced oref1, G3 pre-UAM uncertainty hold, prTrial, twin, antBackout, accelMeal), so stock semantics for SMB minute caps may not map directly to this build.

analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carbohydrate entries, so carb ratios are unvalidatable; no insulin peak time for the free-peak model; no total daily dose series used by dynamic ISF; only 24 sampled statuses for the sensitivity distribution.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are both enabled and, given that carbohydrate entries are absent and COB is always 0, UAM is the only mechanism covering meals; disabling either switch would leave every rise uncovered. The identified problem is gain, not the existence of SMB or UAM. In the activation group, smb_always_enabled true supersedes smb_with_cob_enabled false and smb_after_carbs_enabled false, so those two flags are currently inert but would become live if carbohydrates were logged or if the always flag were turned off. smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled false means a high temporary target suppresses SMB, and the user has set 135 mg/dL temporary targets six times, so this is being used deliberately as a manual brake; the group is internally consistent. In the delivery group, an SMB interval of 3 minutes against a 5-minute CGM cadence is never the binding constraint. The minute caps do not bound observed delivery in this build: on 08-07 the reason string reports standardMaxBolus 0.2 yet microboluses 0.4 U with UAM Boost 1 of 1.23 and UAM Boost 2 of 1.57, and on 08-19 the reason reports UAM High Boost enacted with SMB equal to 1.6 U while IOB was already 4.73 U. Because the UAM minute setting still scales the base that the boosts multiply, max_uam_smb_basal_minutes remains a real but proportional lever, expected to reduce boosted UAM microboluses by roughly a quarter if moved from 20 to 15 minutes, and it acts specifically on the UAM path while leaving the well-controlled 04:00-08:00 local window largely untouched. Regarding compensation: enacted and suggested temp basal rates of 2.32, 2.34, 2.376, 2.7, 3.2, 3.6 and 4.0 U/h against a scheduled 0.5-0.8 U/h mean the loop routinely runs several times the scheduled basal, and on 08-14 it was clamped from a required 5.9 U/h to maxSafeBasal 4 U/h. This is equally explainable by unannounced meals or by daytime basal being set low, so the basal question stays unresolved and no basal change is triggered by automation evidence. Conversely, the 120-minute zero temps after deeply negative guard predictions show the loop braking after the fact, which is the signature of prior over-delivery. User boluses are 0.05 to 0.65 U in 22 of 24 response windows, so essentially all meaningful dosing is automation-driven.
analysis_steps.evidence: decision_inventory groups aaps.core.smb_uam, aaps.core.smb_activation and aaps.core.smb_delivery with all components; representative_loop_statuses (08-07 21:16 standardMaxBolus 0.2 with 0.4 U microbolus; 08-19 15:54 SMB 1.6 U with IOB 4.73; 08-14 18:40 clamp to 4 U/h; 08-11, 08-16 and 08-20 zero temps); representative_events (six temporary targets); therapy_response_windows dose sizes.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Depends on safety_overview (the stacking signature), basal_targets (the unresolved daytime basal question) and profile_cr_isf_dia (the sensitivity spread that the boosts act upon).
analysis_steps.data_gaps: The exact multipliers of the non-stock UAM boosts are not documented in the package, so the magnitude of any change to the UAM minute setting can only be verified empirically; only 24 of 6214 device statuses are exposed.

analysis_steps.findings: The max basal setting of 12 U/h is inert. The binding constraint is the multiplier pair (max_daily_safety_multiplier 5 and current_basal_safety_multiplier 6): the highest profile basal of 0.8 U/h times 5 equals 4.0 U/h, which exactly matches the observed clamp to maxSafeBasal 4 on 08-14. Max IOB of 25 U is likewise non-binding, since the highest observed IOB is 5.935 U, but it is a weak guard-rail at this insulin scale, being well above the observed peak and above any plausible daily dose here. The terminal state quantifies the exposure: 5.935 U of IOB at 245.7 mg/dL implies a fall of about 165 mg/dL when evaluated at the dynamic sensitivity of 27.8 mg/dL per unit, but about 332 mg/dL when evaluated at the profile ISF of 56 mg/dL per unit, so the safety of that state rests entirely on the dynamic estimate being correct. On 08-19 that estimate held (264 to 96 mg/dL at 120 minutes), but on 08-14 it did not (234 to 56 mg/dL at 120 minutes). Because neither ceiling currently binds, tightening them does not alter present-day dosing and does not interact with other changes. The sensitivity group is internally coherent: autosens_enabled false with dynamic_sensitivity_enabled true is the normal dynamic-ISF pattern, and the two autosens target flags being false is consistent with autosens being off. Note that sensitivity_ratio values of 1 in loop statuses are neutral current adjustments, not evidence that autosens is disabled; non-neutral ratios of 0.79, 0.88, 0.91, 0.92, 0.94 and 0.98 also appear. The 70 percent adjustment factor already damps the underlying computation and is a global gain knob, so lowering it further would reduce insulin everywhere, including in the currently excellent 04:00-08:00 local window and against the 13:00-17:00 local time above range of 16.6 to 32.1 percent; it is therefore a blunt instrument for a time-localised problem and it is partially interchangeable with the profile ISF value. The carbohydrate absorption group is currently inert: with no carbohydrate entries and COB 0 throughout, min_5m_carbimpact of 8 mg/dL per 5 minutes and meal_max_absorption_hours of 7 never execute, so no telemetry can support or refute either value. Silently audited items raised only for material reasons: min_carbs_required_grams of 20 is high in a system with 5.1 percent time below range and three level-2 episodes and may suppress early small-carbohydrate prompts, and insulin_type free_peak_oref is paired with DIA 10 hours but no peak time is supplied in the package, so the pairing that governs both IOB decay and dynamic ISF cannot be validated. All six AAPS groups have non-null component values, so no group is eligible for a verify decision.

analysis_steps.data_gaps: Whether total_insulin_u includes basal delivery, which would change the interpretation of max IOB relative to daily dose; the insulin peak time; the internal formula of the non-stock dynamic sensitivity implementation.

analysis_steps.findings: The user-declared strategy record exists and is explicit: analysis_context.source is declared_by_user, declared_at is 2026-08-21T21:08:10, meal_strategies is an empty list, period_exceptions is null and strategy_stable_for_period is null. Because strategy_stable_for_period is not true, the declaration is treated as a real but period-unconfirmed statement, so its applicability and confidence are limited rather than dismissed. Declared strategy and observed execution agree: no prebolus or immediate-bolus-percentage field exists in the package to reproduce, and telemetry contains no meal bolus of any kind. All 24 therapy_response_windows are of type Correction Bolus with is_extended_carbs false, representative_treatments contain only Temp Basal and Correction Bolus events, and 22 of 24 user doses are between 0.05 and 0.65 U. Meal-shaped excursions are therefore descriptions of UAM behaviour around unannounced food rather than of bolus quality. Notable trajectories: on 08-14 from 11:25 local a 0.2 U dose was followed by 100 to 188 to 177 to 197 to 235 to 231 mg/dL, an uncovered rise of 135 mg/dL at 240 minutes; on 08-21 from 13:50 local a 0.35 U dose was followed by 189 to 177 to 206 to 138 to 130 to 123 mg/dL; on 08-14 from 17:20 local a 0.2 U dose preceded 234 to 200 to 56 to 136 to 102 to 61 mg/dL. Two windows contain rises that insulin cannot explain and that indicate unlogged rescue carbohydrate: on 08-12 from 12:40 local, 141 to 71 to 225 mg/dL, a rise of 154 mg/dL in 60 minutes from 71 mg/dL, and on 08-16 from 16:45 local, 206 to 102 to 148 to 53 to 158 mg/dL. This means some measured time above range is hypoglycemia rebound that the loop reads as an unannounced rise and doses into, which both reinforces the over-delivery hypothesis and further blocks carb-ratio inference. Relating the picture to the system: carb ratios were never used, dynamic ISF performs all meal correction with its most aggressive values falling in the 12:00-17:00 local meal band, DIA 10 hours carries that dosing into the 18:00-19:00 and 23:00-03:00 local hypoglycemia clusters, tight targets during unannounced meal hours increase the UAM response, and IOB peaks of 4.73 and 5.935 U occur with COB 0.

analysis_steps.findings: Extended carbohydrates were never used in this period: extended_carb_entries is 0, average_extended_carb_duration_min is null, carb_treatment_entries is an empty list, and is_extended_carbs is false in all 24 response windows. No e-carb amount, start offset or duration exists, so none can be assessed and none is proposed; no duration is inferred from any aggregate, and e-carbs are not treated as equivalent to a pump extended bolus, on which the package also contains no information. The absorption-model parameters that would govern e-carb behaviour, min_5m_carbimpact of 8 mg/dL per 5 minutes and meal_max_absorption_hours of 7, remain inert because COB is 0 throughout, so they cannot be validated. The observed 12:00-17:00 local block does stay elevated for several hours, and one window was still 131 mg/dL above baseline at 360 minutes, which is a prolonged shape that might one day suit extended carbohydrate entry, but with no carbohydrate amount, no meal marker and no composition data, this observation is insufficient to support any e-carb proposal, and meal composition is not invented.

analysis_steps.findings: A contradiction audit against aaps_profile, profile_context and decision_inventory confirms the following and corrects earlier framing. First, the profile is complete and authoritative for the whole period, so no finding may be phrased as a missing profile. Second, the empty meal_strategies list is a declaration with content, not missing data, so prebolus and immediate bolus percentage are not listed as gaps; only the absence of carbohydrate telemetry is a gap. Third, all six AAPS groups have non-null components, so verify is not permissible for any of them and each resolves to change or keep. Fourth, hourly averages reflect delivered insulin, which ranged from 0 to 4 U/h, not the scheduled 0.5-0.8 U/h, so no hourly pattern is converted directly into a basal segment change. Ranking of causes for the dominant pattern, which is afternoon hyperglycemia followed by evening and overnight hypoglycemia: the leading explanation is UAM over-delivery under aggressive high-glucose dynamic sensitivity with a 10-hour insulin tail, supported by microboluses exceeding the computed cap, an explicit high-boost microbolus of 1.6 U on top of 4.73 U of IOB, guard predictions of -4 and -59 mg/dL, repeated 120-minute zero temps, and falls of 178, 168 and 125 mg/dL after doses of 0.65 U or less. A competing explanation, that the basal shape is mistimed with its 0.5 U/h trough at the 16:00 local peak and a rise to 0.7 U/h into the 19:00 local hypoglycemia window, remains plausible and is not separated, because unannounced meals are an equally good account of the same curve. A third explanation, that the early-night basal of 0.6 U/h or the 90 mg/dL target is too low for 23:00-03:00 local, is likewise not separated from the insulin tail. Device events on 08-19 and site or sensor changes on 08-10, 08-11, 08-13, 08-17 and 08-21, plus three GLP-1 doses, contribute to individual days and must be excluded from settings inference. A newly supported factor is unlogged rescue carbohydrate driving a hypoglycemia-rebound-UAM-hypoglycemia oscillation. Because the profile and the automation offer competing accounts of the same curve, the conservative sequence changes nothing in the profile now and instead tightens the two non-binding guard-rails, which cannot alter current dosing, then makes exactly one targeted automation change on the UAM path, then observes, then adds carbohydrate visibility, and only afterwards revisits the interchangeable pair of dynamic-ISF factor and profile ISF and the basal-shape question. No dependent parameters are changed together, and the profile is kept with one precise verification.

strengths: CGM data quality is excellent and supports pattern analysis: 98.7 percent coverage, 5-minute cadence, 3995 valid entries, no invalid, duplicate or out-of-period readings, and a largest gap of only 65 minutes.

Overall glycemic metrics are good: time in range 86.0 percent, mean glucose 121.6 mg/dL, and a coefficient of variation of 32.6 percent, which is below the commonly used 36 percent stability threshold.

The 04:00-08:00 local window is very well controlled, with time in range between 95.8 and 98.7 percent, no time above range, and time below range of 4.8 percent or lower, indicating that the dawn-side basal shape of 0.7 and 0.8 U/h matches this period well.
The AAPS profile is structurally complete, with all basal, carb-ratio, ISF, target, DIA and SMB settings supplied, and profile_context confirms it applied throughout the period.
The user already uses defensive automation controls appropriately, setting 135 mg/dL temporary targets on six occasions, which suppresses SMB under the current activation settings.
Recent days show improving stability: 08-20 reached 90.6 percent in range with only 1.0 percent below range, and 08-21 reached 88.1 percent in range with 0.7 percent below range.
The loop demonstrably applies its own brakes, issuing 120-minute zero temporary basals when guard predictions fall very low.
issues: Time below range of 5.1 percent exceeds the usual 4 percent goal, with three level-2 episodes at 42, 41 and 42 mg/dL, and the hypoglycemia is clustered rather than random.
A recurring evening hypoglycemia cluster at 18:00-19:00 local shows 7.7 and 15.3 percent below range with minima of 42 and 41 mg/dL, and it directly follows the day's highest-glucose block.

A recurring late-night cluster at 23:00-03:00 local shows 10.1 to 18.5 percent below range with spontaneous recovery by 04:00, consistent with an insulin tail, a slightly high early-night basal, or a tight target, which the data do not separate.

The 13:00-17:00 local block carries the highest hyperglycemia burden, with means of 135.0 to 162.8 mg/dL and time above range of 16.6 to 32.1 percent, while the scheduled basal is at its lowest there at 0.5 U/h; unannounced meals remain an equally plausible cause, so this is not attributed to the basal profile.
Insulin-on-board reached 4.73 U and 5.935 U with no carbohydrate on board and user doses of only 0.05 to 0.65 U, indicating that stacking is generated by automation rather than by user bolusing.

Observed microboluses exceed the computed cap in this non-stock build, with 0.4 U delivered against a stated standardMaxBolus of 0.2 U and an explicit high-boost microbolus of 1.6 U issued on top of 4.73 U of existing IOB.

Dynamic sensitivity ranges from 27.8 to 124 mg/dL per unit around a flat profile ISF of 56 mg/dL per unit, and it is most aggressive precisely at the highest glucose values, which is a coherent mechanism for the observed overshoot-then-crash cycle.
Max IOB of 25 U and max basal of 12 U/h never bind at this insulin scale, so the only effective ceilings are the derived maxSafeBasal of 4 U/h and the dynamic sensitivity estimate itself.
No carbohydrate entries exist in the entire period, which blocks validation of all five carb-ratio segments and of the carbohydrate absorption model.

Two response windows show rises that insulin cannot explain, including 71 to 225 mg/dL in 60 minutes, indicating unlogged rescue carbohydrate that the loop then reads as an unannounced rise and doses into.

recommendations.title: Reduce the UAM microbolus strength as the single first therapy-affecting step
recommendations.description: UAM is currently the only meal-handling mechanism, and the evidence points to its strength rather than its existence as the driver of the recurring evening and late-night hypoglycemia. In this build the UAM boosts multiply the computed base, so observed microboluses exceeded the stated cap, with 0.4 U delivered against a standardMaxBolus of 0.2 U and a high-boost microbolus of 1.6 U issued while IOB was already 4.73 U. The consequences appear as falls of 178, 168 and 125 mg/dL after user doses of 0.65 U or less, guard predictions of -4 and -59 mg/dL, repeated 120-minute zero temporary basals, and 18:00-19:00 local time below range of 7.7 and 15.3 percent with minima of 41 and 42 mg/dL. Because max_uam_smb_basal_minutes scales the base that the boosts multiply, reducing it acts proportionally and specifically on the UAM path, while leaving the well-controlled 04:00-08:00 local window largely untouched. This is preferred over the dynamic-ISF factor, which is a global gain knob that would also reduce insulin in the currently good overnight window and against the afternoon hyperglycemia. The accepted trade-off is that afternoon time above range, currently 16.6 to 32.1 percent between 13:00 and 17:00 local, may increase, which is deliberately revisited later against the unresolved basal-shape question.

recommendations.title: Tighten the two non-binding safety ceilings before any dosing change
recommendations.description: Max IOB of 25 U and max basal of 12 U/h never engage: the highest observed IOB is 5.935 U and the effective basal ceiling is already 4.0 U/h, derived from the highest profile basal of 0.8 U/h times the daily safety multiplier of 5, which matches the observed clamp to maxSafeBasal 4 on 08-14. Because neither ceiling binds, moving them closer to the observed operating range does not alter current dosing and does not interact with any other change, which makes it the safest first action in the sequence. Its value is containment: the final status of the window shows 5.935 U of IOB at 245.7 mg/dL, which is safe only if the dynamic sensitivity estimate of 27.8 mg/dL per unit is correct, whereas at the profile ISF of 56 mg/dL per unit the same IOB would imply a much larger fall. Any new ceiling must remain above the observed peak so that normal operation is unchanged, and the two components should be adjusted one at a time.

suggested_change.note: Both components are currently non-binding; keep any new ceiling above the observed peak IOB of 5.935 U so that routine operation is unchanged.
suggested_change.candidate_direction: decrease toward the observed operating range

recommendations.title: Create carbohydrate visibility for one recurring meal and for every hypoglycemia treatment
recommendations.description: With carb_entries 0, total_carbs_g 0.0 and COB 0 in all sampled statuses, five carb-ratio segments and the entire carbohydrate absorption model cannot be validated, and the loop treats every meal as an unannounced rise. Two windows also show rises that insulin cannot explain, including 141 to 71 to 225 mg/dL, indicating unlogged rescue carbohydrate that the loop reads as a fresh rise and doses into. Logging the midday or afternoon meal, which is the most repeatable excursion and the one mechanically upstream of the evening hypoglycemia, plus every hypoglycemia treatment, is the observation that would most improve confidence across the whole analysis. Note that this is not behaviour-neutral: once carbohydrates are entered, smb_with_cob_enabled false, smb_after_carbs_enabled false, min_5m_carbimpact and meal_max_absorption_hours all stop being inert, so the change should be monitored rather than assumed silent, and it should be introduced after the automation steps have been observed.

suggested_change.scope: one recurring meal at approximately 12:00-15:00 local, plus all hypoglycemia treatments
suggested_change.action: log carbohydrate amount and entry time only; do not add a prebolus, an immediate bolus percentage or extended carbohydrates during this phase

recommendations.title: Defer the choice between the dynamic ISF factor and the profile ISF until after the UAM observation
recommendations.description: Dynamic sensitivity ranged from 27.8 to 124 mg/dL per unit around a flat profile ISF of 56 mg/dL per unit, driven by dynamic sensitivity enabled at a 70 percent adjustment factor with autosens disabled. These two settings act on the same output and are partially interchangeable, so changing either now, and certainly both, would make the effect of the UAM change uninterpretable. In addition, the 70 percent factor is a global gain knob that would reduce insulin in the currently excellent 04:00-08:00 local window and against the 13:00-17:00 local time above range, which makes it a poor first instrument for a time-localised problem. This item is included only because it defines the safe order: it must come after the UAM delivery change and after carbohydrate visibility exists.

revisit_after: carbohydrate logging for one recurring meal

recommendations.title: Keep all basal and target segments and test the afternoon and evening question with data, not with a change
recommendations.description: The afternoon block shows the lowest scheduled basal at 0.5 U/h alongside the highest time above range at 16.6 to 32.1 percent, and the evening block adds basal at 0.6 and 0.7 U/h into a falling limb that ends in 15.3 percent time below range. This pairing is suggestive, but delivered temp basal rates ranged from 0 to 4.0 U/h against a scheduled 0.5-0.8 U/h, so hourly averages measure automation output rather than the basal profile, and with zero carbohydrate entries unannounced meals explain the same curve equally well. The same applies overnight, where the 23:00-03:00 local pattern is equally consistent with a 10-hour insulin tail, a slightly high 0.6 U/h basal, or the tight 90 mg/dL target. Changing basal or targets now would be changing a parameter that is competing with an unresolved automation explanation. The correct next action is the observation defined above, after which the afternoon and evening segments can be reassessed with the automation contribution reduced and with meals visible.

suggested_change.action: keep all seven basal segments and all three target segments unchanged
reassess_after: carbohydrate logging for one recurring meal
competing_explanations_to_separate: UAM over-delivery with a 10-hour insulin tail

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep all seven basal segments, all three target segments, all five carb-ratio segments, the flat ISF of 56 mg/dL per unit and the DIA of 10 hours unchanged for now, and address the hypoglycemia clusters through the automation sequence first, starting with the non-binding safety ceilings and then a single reduction of the UAM microbolus strength.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Every candidate profile change competes with an automation explanation that the current data cannot exclude. The afternoon block has the lowest scheduled basal at 0.5 U/h and the highest time above range at 16.6 to 32.1 percent, and the evening block raises basal to 0.6 and 0.7 U/h into a falling limb ending at 15.3 percent time below range with minima of 41 and 42 mg/dL, yet delivered temp basal rates in the sample ranged from 0 to 4.0 U/h, so the observed curve reflects automation output rather than the scheduled basal. With carb_entries 0 and COB 0 throughout, unannounced meals explain the same afternoon rise equally well. Overnight, the 23:00-03:00 local pattern with recovery by 04:00 is equally consistent with the 10-hour insulin tail, a slightly high 0.6 U/h basal and the tight 90 mg/dL target. The dawn-side segments are demonstrably correct, with 95.8 to 98.7 percent time in range between 04:00 and 08:00 local. Carb ratios were never exercised, so no carb-ratio change has any supporting evidence, and the flat ISF is partially interchangeable with the 70 percent dynamic-ISF factor, so changing it now would confound the automation observation.
profile_recommendation.next_check: After the UAM delivery change has run for 10 days without any other modification, compare time below range at 18:00-19:00 local and at 23:00-03:00 local against the current 7.7, 15.3, 10.1, 11.4, 18.5, 10.1 and 10.2 percent, and compare time above range at 13:00-17:00 local against the current 16.6 to 32.1 percent; if the evening and overnight time below range falls toward 4 percent or lower while afternoon time above range rises, the pattern was automation-driven and the basal profile stays unchanged, whereas if the evening time below range persists at 15:00-19:00 local levels the 18:00 and 19:00 basal segments become the next candidate for a single-segment review.

parameter_decisions.rationale: The 00:00-05:00 local block shows time below range of 11.4, 18.5, 10.1 and 10.2 percent at hours 23, 1, 2 and 3 local with means of 93.3, 90.6, 101.9 and 104.7 mg/dL and spontaneous recovery by 04:00, which is a real pattern. However, the evidence does not separate three competing causes: an insulin tail under the 10-hour DIA, the 0.6 U/h basal itself, and the tight 90 mg/dL target that leaves no buffer. Delivered temp basal in this window ranged from 0 to nearly 2 U/h in the sample, so the hourly average does not measure the scheduled rate. Uncertainty is further raised by IOB peaks of 2.80 and 5.935 U late in the evening. This segment is dependent on the outcome of the UAM delivery change and cannot be adjusted at the same time.

The 05:00-06:00 local window performs well, with a mean of 104.2 mg/dL, 95.2 percent time in range, 4.8 percent time below range and no time above range. There is no evidence of a defect, and any change here would risk the best-controlled part of the day. Uncertainty is low for this segment; the only caveat is that the isolated 42 mg/dL at 07:19 local on 08-21 sits nearby, which is monitored rather than acted upon. No dependency requires a change.

The 06:00-10:00 local block is the strongest of the day, with means of 99.5, 99.5, 110.5 and 132.9 mg/dL and time in range of 97.5, 98.7, 98.2 and 91.1 percent, with time below range of 2.5, 1.3, 0.0 and 0.0 percent. This segment is validated by the data and should be preserved as a reference for the rest of the analysis. The only uncertainty is that the 09:00-10:00 local rise begins here and may be meal-related, which cannot be resolved without carbohydrate entries.

The 10:00-16:00 local block shows rising means from 148.0 to 162.8 mg/dL with time above range from 20.2 to 32.1 percent, which could suggest insufficient basal. However, carb_entries is 0 and COB is 0 in all sampled statuses, so unannounced meals are at least as plausible, and delivered temp basal in this window reached 2.7 to 4.0 U/h, several times the scheduled rate, which means the loop was not constrained by this segment. Raising basal here would also add insulin upstream of the 18:00-19:00 local hypoglycemia cluster, which is the opposite of the current safety priority. Dependent on carbohydrate visibility and on the UAM change before reassessment.

This segment coincides with the worst hyperglycemia of the day, 162.8 mg/dL mean and 32.1 percent time above range at 16:00 local, while carrying the lowest scheduled rate of the profile, which makes it the most tempting change in the package. It is withheld for three reasons: unannounced meals explain the same rise with zero carbohydrate entries, the loop already overrode this segment with temp basals up to 4.0 U/h and was clamped at maxSafeBasal on 08-14, and increasing insulin here would feed directly into the 18:00-19:00 local hypoglycemia cluster with minima of 41 and 42 mg/dL. It is also the segment most likely to have been set low deliberately for unrecorded afternoon activity. This is the highest-priority profile candidate for reassessment once the UAM change and carbohydrate logging are in place.

This segment adds basal into a falling limb: means drop from 148.9 to 124.2 mg/dL at 18:00 local with 7.7 percent time below range and a minimum of 42 mg/dL, and two of the three level-2 episodes occur at 18:00-19:15 local. A reduction is therefore directionally plausible. It is withheld because the leading explanation is the insulin tail from afternoon UAM dosing under a 10-hour DIA rather than the scheduled 0.6 U/h, evidenced by falls of 178 and 125 mg/dL after user doses of 0.2 U, and because changing this segment simultaneously with the UAM delivery change would make neither effect interpretable. This is the second profile candidate for reassessment if the evening hypoglycemia persists after the automation step.

The 19:00 local hour carries the highest time below range of the entire day at 15.3 percent with a minimum of 41 mg/dL, while the scheduled basal rises to its joint-highest daytime value. This is a genuine mismatch in direction. The change is withheld for the same reason as the 18:00 segment: the 08-14 sequence of 234 to 200 to 56 mg/dL after a 0.2 U dose shows automation, not scheduled basal, driving the fall, and the two settings must not be changed together. If the evening cluster survives the UAM reduction, this segment and the 18:00 segment become the primary review targets, one at a time.

This carb ratio was never exercised during the period: carb_entries is 0, total_carbs_g is 0.0, carb_treatment_entries is empty and COB is 0 in all 24 sampled loop statuses, so the value appears only as profile read-back inside loop reason strings. There is no evidence in either direction, so keep is the correct status rather than any change. Dependent on carbohydrate logging becoming available before any assessment is possible.

No carbohydrate was entered at any time in the 14-day window, so this segment produced no dosing and cannot be validated or refuted. The 04:00-08:00 local window is in any case the best-controlled part of the day on basal alone. Keep, dependent on future carbohydrate entries.

Unvalidatable for the same reason: zero carbohydrate entries and COB 0 throughout mean this ratio never contributed insulin. The morning rise from 110.5 to 148.0 mg/dL between 08:00 and 10:00 local was handled entirely by UAM, so it carries no information about the carb ratio. Keep, dependent on carbohydrate logging.

This is the strongest carb ratio in the profile and covers the worst hyperglycemia block, but with zero carbohydrate entries it was never applied, so the 32.1 percent time above range at 16:00 local says nothing about its correctness. No change is supportable. Keep, dependent on carbohydrate logging for the recurring afternoon meal, which is the designated next observation.

Never exercised during the period, as with all other carb-ratio segments. The evening pattern in this window is dominated by the falling limb from the afternoon and by insulin tail effects, not by carbohydrate dosing. Keep, dependent on carbohydrate logging.

The single flat ISF segment is not used directly, because dynamic sensitivity is enabled with a 70 percent adjustment factor and rescaled the effective value across a 4.5-fold range from 27.8 to 124 mg/dL per unit in the sampled statuses. This makes the profile ISF and the dynamic-ISF adjustment factor partially interchangeable levers on the same output, so changing this value now would confound the planned automation observation and it is explicitly excluded from being changed together with the sensitivity group. There is also a material safety consideration: at the terminal status, 5.935 U of IOB implies a fall of about 165 mg/dL at the dynamic value of 27.8 but about 332 mg/dL at the profile value of 56, so the correct choice between the two levers requires the post-change observation. Keep for now; this is the designated third decision point in the sequence.

A target of 90 mg/dL through the 00:00-08:00 local block is tight and coincides with 18.5, 10.1 and 10.2 percent time below range in the first hours, which makes a small increase directionally plausible. It is withheld because the same overnight pattern is equally explained by the 10-hour insulin tail from evening automation, because the 04:00-08:00 portion of the same segment performs excellently at 95.2 to 98.7 percent time in range, and because a target change would alter loop behaviour at the same time as the planned UAM change. Dependent on the outcome of that observation.

The 100 mg/dL daytime target applies across both the best-performing morning hours and the worst afternoon hours, so the hourly data give no consistent signal about it. Effective targets in the sampled statuses already varied between 80 and 116 mg/dL, and the user applied 135 mg/dL temporary targets six times, which is a more flexible instrument than a standing target change and is already in use. No change is supportable; dependent on the automation observation.

The 23:00 local hour shows 11.4 percent time below range with a mean of 105.7 mg/dL, and this segment sets a 90 mg/dL target immediately before the deepest overnight cluster, so it is a plausible contributor. It is withheld because the cause is not separated from the insulin tail and the 0.6 U/h basal that begins one hour later, and because changing the target and the UAM strength together would be uninterpretable. This segment is reassessed together with the 00:00 basal segment after the automation observation.

A 10-hour DIA is long and is a plausible contributor to the prolonged declines observed at 240 to 360 minutes after very small doses, such as 125 to 57 mg/dL at 240 minutes and 75 mg/dL at 360 minutes on 08-17, and 206 to 53 mg/dL at 180 minutes on 08-16. However, those windows contain concurrent temp basal and microbolus delivery, so they demonstrate net system action rather than the insulin curve, and no insulin peak time is supplied in the package despite insulin_type free_peak_oref, so the DIA and peak pairing cannot be validated. A longer DIA is also conservative for IOB accounting, meaning a reduction could increase rather than decrease dosing. No change is supportable on this evidence; dependent on the peak time being clarified with the care team.

Both components are present and non-null, so verify is not applicable. With zero carbohydrate entries and COB 0 in every sampled status, UAM is the only mechanism covering meals, and disabling either switch would leave every rise uncovered and would predictably worsen the 13:00-17:00 local block that already runs at 16.6 to 32.1 percent time above range. The identified problem is delivery gain, not the existence of SMB or UAM, and the gain is addressed in the delivery group instead. Uncertainty is low for this decision; the dependency is that the delivery group change must be the one that carries the effect.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / SMB activation conditions (smb_always_enabled, smb_with_cob_enabled, smb_after_carbs_enabled, smb_with_temp_target_enabled, smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled)
parameter_decisions.rationale: All five components are non-null, so verify is not applicable. The group is internally consistent: smb_always_enabled true currently supersedes smb_with_cob_enabled false and smb_after_carbs_enabled false, which are therefore inert while no carbohydrates are entered, and smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled false gives the user a working manual brake that was used six times through 135 mg/dL temporary targets, including two 180-minute periods. No component change is supported by the data. The dependency to note is that the two currently inert flags become active as soon as carbohydrate logging begins, so this group must be re-examined at that point rather than assumed unchanged.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / SMB strength and frequency (smb_interval_minutes, max_smb_basal_minutes, max_uam_smb_basal_minutes)
parameter_decisions.rationale: Only one component is proposed for change: max_uam_smb_basal_minutes from 20 min to 15 min. Evidence: UAM is the sole meal-handling path, and observed microboluses exceeded the computed cap in this non-stock build, with 0.4 U delivered against a stated standardMaxBolus of 0.2 U under UAM Boost values of 1.23 and 1.57, and a high-boost microbolus of 1.6 U issued while IOB was already 4.73 U. Downstream consequences are falls of 178, 168 and 125 mg/dL after user doses of 0.65 U or less, guard predictions of -4 and -59 mg/dL with 120-minute zero temporary basals, IOB peaks of 4.73 and 5.935 U with COB 0, and evening time below range of 7.7 and 15.3 percent with minima of 41 and 42 mg/dL. Because the UAM minute setting scales the base that the boosts multiply, the change acts proportionally and specifically on the UAM path and leaves the excellent 04:00-08:00 local window largely untouched. Uncertainty: the build-specific boost multipliers are not documented in the package, so the magnitude is approximate and must be verified empirically, and afternoon time above range may increase. Dependencies: smb_interval_minutes of 3 min is never binding against a 5-minute CGM cadence and stays unchanged, max_smb_basal_minutes of 15 min governs the non-UAM path and stays unchanged, and this change must not be combined with any sensitivity, ISF, basal or target change.
parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=15 min

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits (max_basal_u_per_hour, max_iob_units)
parameter_decisions.rationale: Both components are non-null, so verify is not applicable, and both are currently non-binding, which is exactly why changing them is safe and comes first. Evidence: the highest observed IOB is 5.935 U against a ceiling of 25 U, and the effective basal ceiling is already 4.0 U/h, derived from the highest profile basal of 0.8 U/h multiplied by max_daily_safety_multiplier 5, confirmed by the observed clamp of a required 5.9 U/h to maxSafeBasal 4 on 08-14, so the configured 12 U/h never engages. Proposed direction: reduce max_iob_units from 25 U to 10 U, which remains comfortably above the observed peak of 5.935 U and therefore does not alter routine dosing, and afterwards align max_basal_u_per_hour from 12 U/h to 5 U/h, which remains above the effective 4.0 U/h clamp. Rationale for containment: at the terminal status the safety of 5.935 U of IOB depends entirely on the dynamic sensitivity estimate of 27.8 mg/dL per unit being correct, and on 08-14 a comparable estimate failed, producing a fall to 56 mg/dL. Uncertainty: it is not stated whether total_insulin_u of 275.95 U includes basal delivery, so the ceiling relative to total daily dose cannot be computed precisely, which is why the proposed values sit well above observed operation. Dependency: change the two components one at a time, max_iob_units first, and complete both before the UAM delivery change.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / Autosens and Dynamic ISF (autosens_enabled, dynamic_sensitivity_enabled, autosens_raises_target, autosens_lowers_target, dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent)
parameter_decisions.rationale: All five components are non-null, so verify is not applicable. The configuration is internally coherent: autosens_enabled false with dynamic_sensitivity_enabled true is the normal dynamic-ISF arrangement, and both autosens target flags being false is consistent with autosens being off. Sensitivity_ratio values of 1 in the loop statuses are read as neutral current adjustments and not as evidence about the switch, and non-neutral ratios of 0.79, 0.88, 0.91, 0.92, 0.94 and 0.98 also appear. Behaviourally, dynamic sensitivity ranged from 27.8 to 124 mg/dL per unit and was most aggressive at the highest glucose values, which is a coherent mechanism for the overshoot-then-crash cycle, so a reduction of the 70 percent factor is directionally plausible. It is withheld because the factor is a global gain knob that would also reduce insulin in the currently excellent 04:00-08:00 local window and against the 13:00-17:00 local time above range of 16.6 to 32.1 percent, and because it is partially interchangeable with profile.isf.00_00, so the two must never be changed together and the choice between them requires the post-UAM observation. Dependent on the delivery-group change being observed first.

Both components are non-null, so verify is not applicable. Both are currently inert: with carb_entries 0, total_carbs_g 0.0, extended_carb_entries 0 and COB 0 in all 24 sampled statuses, the carbohydrate decay floor of 8 mg/dL per 5 minutes and the absorption expiry of 7 hours never execute, so no telemetry can support or refute either value and changing an inert parameter would only add noise. Uncertainty: meal_max_absorption_hours of 7 is above the common default, which may matter once carbohydrates are entered, but no meal-linked evidence exists and no duration is inferred from any aggregate. Dependency: this group becomes assessable at the same moment that carbohydrate logging unblocks the five carb-ratio segments, and it must be re-reviewed then.

meal_strategy_summary.rationale: The user-declared strategy record is present and explicit, with source declared_by_user, declared at 2026-08-21T21:08:10, an empty meal_strategies list, period_exceptions null and strategy_stable_for_period null. Because strategy_stable_for_period is not true, this is treated as a genuine declaration with limited period confirmation rather than as missing data, and no prebolus or immediate-bolus-percentage field exists in the package to reproduce. The declaration and the telemetry agree: all 24 therapy response windows are correction boluses with is_extended_carbs false, representative treatments contain only temp basals and correction boluses, 22 of 24 user doses are between 0.05 and 0.65 U, and carb_entries is 0 with COB 0 in every sampled status, so meals are handled entirely by UAM. This agreement is the most reliable meal-domain finding. The excursion shape shows a repeating midday and afternoon rise from 141.3 to 162.8 mg/dL between 12:00 and 16:00 local with time above range up to 32.1 percent, followed within two to four hours by the evening hypoglycemia cluster at 7.7 and 15.3 percent below range with minima of 41 and 42 mg/dL, and one window rose 135 mg/dL by 240 minutes despite a 0.2 U dose. Two windows also show rises that insulin cannot explain, 71 to 225 mg/dL in 60 minutes and 53 to 158 mg/dL in 60 minutes, indicating unlogged hypoglycemia treatment that the loop reads as a fresh rise and doses into. Adding front-loaded meal insulin in this state would compound the existing hypoglycemia burden of 5.1 percent with three level-2 episodes and IOB peaks near 6 U, so visibility must precede any meal-dosing change.

exceptions.pattern: Recurring midday and afternoon excursion between 12:00 and 17:00 local, with means of 135.0 to 162.8 mg/dL, time above range of 16.6 to 32.1 percent, both 285-293 mg/dL clusters, and the evening hypoglycemia cluster following two to four hours later
exceptions.rationale: This is the only consistently recurring excursion block and it is mechanically upstream of the largest hypoglycemia risk, so it yields the most information for the least added risk, and it is the observation that would separate the UAM over-delivery explanation from the afternoon basal-shape explanation that currently compete for the same curve.
exceptions.suggestion: Make this the first and only meal to log with an approximate carbohydrate amount and entry time, and observe it for at least ten days before considering any dosing change in this window

exceptions.pattern: Post-hypoglycemia rebound highs, seen on 08-12 from 12:40 local as 141 to 71 to 225 mg/dL and on 08-16 from 16:45 local as 206 to 102 to 148 to 53 to 158 mg/dL, with no carbohydrate record
exceptions.rationale: The loop currently interprets these rebounds as unannounced meals and doses UAM into them, which feeds the next low, and the missing records also inflate measured time above range and would corrupt any future carb-ratio assessment.
exceptions.suggestion: Log every hypoglycemia treatment as a carbohydrate entry with its amount and time

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Keep meals fully UAM-driven for now and add nothing that increases insulin delivery: introduce no prebolus and set no immediate bolus percentage, since no such value is declared or observable and proposing one would be unsupported; leave SMB and UAM enabled as the only meal-handling path while their strength is reduced once through the UAM microbolus setting; and do not use extended carbohydrates, since none were ever entered and no amount, start offset or duration exists to assess. Instead, make meals visible by logging an approximate carbohydrate amount at the start of the single most repeatable meal each day, around 12:00 to 15:00 local, and by logging every hypoglycemia treatment, and note that this is not behaviour-neutral because entering carbohydrates activates the currently inert settings smb_with_cob_enabled, smb_after_carbs_enabled, min_5m_carbimpact and meal_max_absorption_hours.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Record the carbohydrate grams and the entry time for the midday or afternoon meal on seven to ten consecutive days while keeping dosing behaviour otherwise unchanged; this single observation unblocks carb-ratio validation, gives the loop carbohydrate on board so that meal and UAM effects can be separated, tests the competing explanations for the 13:00-17:00 local hyperglycemia and the 18:00-19:00 local hypoglycemia, and makes the carbohydrate absorption model assessable, all without increasing insulin delivery.

implementation_steps: Step 0, before any change: review this analysis with the care team, confirm that the 41, 42 and 42 mg/dL episodes on 08-13, 08-14 and 08-21 were recognised and treated, and agree how hypoglycemia treatment will be recorded from now on.

Step 1, data hygiene with no therapy change: note that the occlusion and pump error on 08-19, the site changes on 08-10, 08-13 and 08-17, the sensor changes on 08-11 and 08-21, and the GLP-1 doses on 08-14, 08-17 and 08-20 all fall inside this window, and exclude those days from any future settings comparison.

Step 2, clarify two facts that change interpretation but require no change now: whether the reported 275.95 U of insulin includes basal delivery, and what insulin peak time is configured alongside the free-peak model and the 10-hour DIA.

Step 3, first change, behaviour-neutral containment: reduce max_iob_units from 25 U toward approximately 10 U, keeping it well above the observed peak of 5.935 U so that routine dosing is unchanged, and observe for three to five days that no dosing behaviour has altered.

Step 4, second change, still containment: align max_basal_u_per_hour from 12 U/h toward approximately 5 U/h, keeping it above the effective 4.0 U/h clamp that already applies, and confirm over three to five days that temporary basal delivery is unchanged.
Step 5, the primary therapy-affecting change, one component only: reduce max_uam_smb_basal_minutes from 20 min to 15 min, and change nothing else at the same time.

Step 6, observe step 5 for at least ten days and record four numbers for comparison: time below range at 18:00-19:00 local against the current 7.7 and 15.3 percent, time below range at 23:00-03:00 local against the current 10.1 to 18.5 percent, peak IOB with no carbohydrate on board against the current 5.935 U, and time above range at 13:00-17:00 local against the current 16.6 to 32.1 percent.

Step 7, add carbohydrate visibility without changing dosing: log an approximate carbohydrate amount and time for one recurring midday or afternoon meal and for every hypoglycemia treatment, for seven to ten days, while monitoring that the newly activated settings smb_with_cob_enabled, smb_after_carbs_enabled, min_5m_carbimpact and meal_max_absorption_hours do not produce unexpected behaviour.

Step 8, only after steps 5 to 7 have been observed, decide between exactly one of the two interchangeable sensitivity levers, either dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent or the flat profile ISF of 56 mg/dL per unit, and never both.

Step 9, only if evening hypoglycemia persists after step 6, review the 19:00 basal segment first and the 18:00 segment second, one segment at a time with at least ten days of observation between them.

Step 10, only if overnight hypoglycemia at 23:00-03:00 local persists, review either the 00:00 basal segment or the 23:00 target segment, one at a time, and only after the insulin-tail contribution has been reduced.

education: Time in range of 86.0 percent and a coefficient of variation of 32.6 percent are both at or better than commonly cited goals, while time below range of 5.1 percent is above the usual 4 percent goal; when hypoglycemia is concentrated in specific hours rather than spread evenly, the pattern usually points to a specific mechanism rather than to a general excess of insulin.

Hourly glucose averages reflect what the automation actually delivered, not what the basal profile scheduled; in this period the loop delivered between 0 and 4.0 U/h against a scheduled 0.5 to 0.8 U/h, which is why a high or low hour cannot be read directly as a basal error.

When dynamic sensitivity is enabled, the profile ISF becomes a base value that the algorithm rescales continuously; here the effective value ranged from 27.8 to 124 mg/dL per unit around a profile value of 56, so the profile ISF and the dynamic adjustment factor act on the same output and adjusting both at once makes the result impossible to interpret.

A longer duration of insulin action means more insulin is counted as still active, which is conservative for insulin-on-board accounting, but it also means dosing decisions carry a longer tail, so a rise handled aggressively in the afternoon can still be lowering glucose several hours later.

Unannounced-meal handling covers rises after they begin rather than before, which typically produces a higher peak followed by a later fall; without carbohydrate entries the algorithm cannot distinguish a meal rise from a rebound after a low, so unlogged hypoglycemia treatment can be interpreted as a new meal and dosed into.

Extended carbohydrate entries in AAPS shape the algorithm's carbohydrate-on-board and prediction curves and are not the same thing as a pump extended bolus; they can only be evaluated once ordinary carbohydrate entries exist to establish an absorption pattern.

A safety limit that never engages provides no protection; when the highest observed insulin-on-board is 5.935 U, a 25 U ceiling has no practical effect, and adjusting such a limit closer to real operation changes nothing in daily use while restoring a meaningful boundary.

Changing one setting at a time and allowing roughly ten days of observation is what makes it possible to attribute an improvement or a deterioration to that specific change, particularly when several settings could explain the same pattern.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only and not medical advice. Every proposed change must be independently verified with the responsible care team before it is applied.
Make only one change at a time, apply it manually, and monitor glucose closely afterwards; nothing here should be applied automatically to AAPS.

Three level-2 hypoglycemia episodes occurred in this period, at 42 mg/dL on 08-13, 41 mg/dL on 08-14 and 42 mg/dL on 08-21, and time below range of 5.1 percent is above the usual 4 percent goal; reducing hypoglycemia takes priority over reducing the 13:00-17:00 local hyperglycemia, and an increase in afternoon time above range is an accepted short-term trade-off.

The final reading in the period shows 245.7 mg/dL rising with 5.935 U of insulin on board and a requested rate of 4 U/h, which is a substantial forward hypoglycemia exposure after the data end and warrants close monitoring independently of any setting change.

No rescue-carbohydrate records exist anywhere in the package, so it cannot be established whether the lowest readings were treated; agreeing a hypoglycemia treatment and recording routine with the care team is a prerequisite for interpreting any future data.

The setting min_carbs_required_grams of 20 g is high in a system with this hypoglycemia burden and may suppress early small-carbohydrate prompts; this is raised for discussion with the care team rather than as a tuning proposal.

The loop reason strings contain non-standard markers including UAM Boost, UAM High Boost enacted, Enhanced oref1 and other build-specific fields, and observed microboluses exceeded the computed cap, so standard expectations about the effect size of SMB settings may not apply to this build and every change must be verified by observation rather than assumed.

Device events inside this period, namely the occlusion and pump error on 08-19, three site changes and two sensor changes, plus three GLP-1 doses, can each produce glucose patterns that resemble a settings problem; individual days affected by these events should not be used as evidence for or against any parameter change.
